claim: MUI ships an official Tailwind CSS v4 integration guide requiring enableCssLayer plus a manual @layer order declaration so mui precedes utilities.
quote: enableCssLayer: true ensures Material UI styles are wrapped in @layer mui, which allows Tailwind CSS v4 utilities to override them predictably. ... @layer theme, base, mui, components, utilities;

claim: MUI's older style-library-interoperability guide is the Tailwind v3-era recipe: StyledEngineProvider injectFirst, preflight:false, important:'#root'/'#__next'.
quote: To reduce the need for the important property, you need to change the CSS injection order [wrap with <StyledEngineProvider injectFirst>] ... Add the important option, using the id of your app wrapper

claim: MUI maintainers acknowledged that MUI v6 selectors exceed (0,1,0) specificity and that Tailwind v4's native layers make MUI unoverridable without a configurable layer; fix landed via a Stylis plugin emitting @layer mui.
quote: some components have higher CSS specificity than (0,1,0) so Tailwind CSS could not be used without !important ... Tailwind v4 is using native CSS layer so Material UI won't be able to override it without a configurable layer

claim: Jan 2025 docs issue: users found Tailwind v4 utilities like m-2 silently not applying against MUI because MUI's Emotion CSS is unlayered while utilities sit in @layer utilities; closed as duplicate of #44700.
quote: TailwindCSS released a new version recently, but the docs show integration guide with an older version ... utility classes are not being applied because of cascade errors related to using CSS layers

claim: PR adding enableCssLayer to StyledEngineProvider (merged 12 Mar 2025, backported to v6.x); it is independent of injectFirst and still requires manual GlobalStyles layer-order declaration.
quote: Added a new `enableCssLayer` prop (same prop name as the AppRouter integration) ... Users must manually configure CSS layer ordering via GlobalStyles

claim: MUI's modularCssLayers splits styles into mui.global / mui.components / mui.theme / mui.custom / mui.sx, and MUI warns that enabling it in an existing app changes specificity and can visibly break the UI.
quote: Cascade layers let you control the order of the styles, which can help avoid specificity conflicts. ... unexpected changes to the look and feel of the UI [theme style overrides may suddenly take precedence where they previously had no effect]

claim: MUI's own agent skill file codifies the recipe: layer order line before @import 'tailwindcss', enableCssLayer per framework, and for v3 preflight:false + important:'#root' + injectFirst.
quote:
@layer theme, base, mui, components, utilities;
@import 'tailwindcss'; ... corePlugins: { preflight: false } so MUI CssBaseline owns base resets

claim: July 2026 Tailwind discussion on specificity wars with third-party component libraries: unlayered CSS beats layered CSS regardless of specificity; MUI v6+ can opt into a layer, raw Emotion/styled-components cannot.
quote: unlayered CSS beats layered CSS regardless of specificity ... MUI v6+ can emit into a layer via <StyledEngineProvider enableCssLayer>, while raw emotion and styled-components cannot easily participate in cascade layers

claim: Dec 2024 discussion 'Tailwind 4.0 not usable with any system that provides its own styles' — host/global unlayered styles beat v4 utilities; no maintainer answer, community workaround is to import utilities.css WITHOUT a layer.
quote: Due to the final `styles.css` file retaining the layers, the default global styles of Obsidian overrule tailwind utilities

claim: Tailwind v4 removed the JS `important` config option; collaborator wongjn's answer is to hand-roll layer imports instead (Jan 2025, 17 replies).
quote: You'd replace the `@import "tailwindcss";` with: @layer theme, base, components, utilities; @import "tailwindcss/theme.css" layer(theme)...

claim: The v4 replacement for `important: true` is the CSS-first `@import "tailwindcss" important;` (collaborator wongjn, 13 May 2025); per-utility form moved to trailing bang (bg-red-500!).
quote: You can add the `important` tag to the Tailwind import: @import "tailwindcss" important;

claim: Tailwind v4 dropped corePlugins (so `corePlugins: { preflight: false }` is gone) and moved the important modifier to the end of the class name.
quote: In v3 there was a `corePlugins` option you could use to completely disable certain utilities in the framework. This is no longer supported in v4. ... The `corePlugins`, `safelist`, and `separator` options from the JavaScript-based config are not supported in v4.0.

claim: In Tailwind v4 preflight is disabled by omitting the preflight.css import, and preflight zeroes margins/padding, unstyles headings and lists, and resets borders — all of which double up with MUI CssBaseline.
Emotion has no built-in way to wrap its generated CSS in a cascade layer; the request is still open since Nov 2023, labelled documentation/needs-triage.
quote: I would love to wrap all the generated emotion CSS with `@layer framework { styles}` and don't know how.

claim: styled-components likewise lacks cascade-layer support: @layer inside a styled block emits the at-rule without the generated class selector (opened Feb 2023, closed).
quote: I tried to play around with cascade layers and noticed that styled-components did not seems to have support for it.

claim: Independent confirmation of the same class of bug in another kit: runtime-injected unlayered stylesheets overwrite Tailwind v4 utilities because unlayered declarations outrank layered ones.
quote: Tailwind CSS v4 is built on native cascade layers. This unfortunately breaks some Flux components because the injected stylesheets overwrite the utilities because unlayered declarations have a higher priority than layered declarations.

claim: Long-running community thread on MUI+Tailwind (2023-2024): Tailwind classes appear not to apply at all next to MUI; advice was prefix + important config flags, or 'use a Tailwind-native kit instead'.
quote: you can achieve it by using the prefix and the important config flags. This helps with css namespace conflicts.

claim: Shipped-app postmortem (28 Jul 2025): MUI Emotion styles outranked Tailwind utilities in production; fix was to pick one system per concern and use Tailwind v4 layers.
quote: components misaligned, text sizes changed, layouts distorted ... Material UI's Emotion-generated styles had higher CSS specificity, overriding Tailwind utilities even when explicitly applied

claim: Steelman: Infinum's engineering handbook treats Tailwind + MUI coexistence as a supported pattern (Tailwind for layout, MUI theme for stateful styles) provided import order and CSS-variable theming are set up.
quote: Make sure `tailwind.css` is imported after any baseline or component library stylesheet so its utilities win specificity ties.

claim: Explainer (16 Apr 2026) of the v4 cascade rule that bites CSS-in-JS: anything outside @layer sits above every named layer and always wins.
quote: Any CSS rule written outside a `@layer` declaration is implicitly placed above all named layers in the cascade. ... The spec calls this the 'unlayered' context, and it always wins.

claim: Feb 2026 comparison frames Tailwind and MUI as competing philosophies rather than complements; specificity conflicts cited as a scale problem.
quote: For small projects, this is manageable. For SaaS products, dashboards, and enterprise apps — it becomes expensive.
